questions.question: Ramani sells her car to Sarla at a loss of 15%. If Sarla pays ₹1,91,250 for it, then what is the cost price of the car for Ramani?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramani sells her car to Sarla at a loss of 15%.

Sarla pays ₹1,91,250 for the car.

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (C.P.) = Selling Price (S.P.) / (1 - Loss%)

**Calculation:**

Loss% = 15% = 15 / 100 = 0.15

⇒ Cost Price (C.P.) = ₹1,91,250 / (1 - 0.15)

⇒ C.P. = ₹1,91,250 / 0.85

⇒ C.P. = ₹2,25,000

**The cost price of the car for Ramani is ₹2,25,000.**

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and their HCF is 60. The numbers are:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three numbers are in the ratio 3:4:5.

The HCF of the three numbers is 60.

**Formula Used:**

Numbers = (HCF × Ratio).

**Calculation:**

The numbers are given in the ratio 3:4:5 and their HCF is 60.

⇒ First Number = 60 × 3 = 180

⇒ Second Number = 60 × 4 = 240

⇒ Third Number = 60 × 5 = 300

**The numbers are 180, 240, and 300.**

questions.question: In a park there are rabbits and pigeons in the ratio 4 : 9. If legs are counted, the total number of legs is 340. Find the number of rabbits.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Rabbits : Pigeons = 4 : 9

Ratio of their legs = (4 × 4) : (9 × 2) = 16 : 18

Total proportional legs = 16 + 18 = 34 units

Given total legs = 340 ⇒ 1 unit = 340 ÷ 34 = 10

Number of rabbits = 4 units × 10 = 40

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Rabbits to Pigeons = 4 : 9

Total number of legs = 340

**Formula Used:**

Total Legs = (Number of Rabbits × 4) + (Number of Pigeons × 2)

 
 Rabbits (4x)
 Ratio 4
 
 
 Pigeons (9x)
 Ratio 9
 
 
• 
 
 Legs per Rabbit = 4
 Legs per Pigeon = 2
 
 Total Legs = 340

Let the common multiplier be x.

⇒ Number of rabbits = 4x

⇒ Number of pigeons = 9x

⇒ Total legs = (4x × 4) + (9x × 2)

⇒ 340 = 16x + 18x

⇒ 340 = 34x

⇒ x = 340 ÷ 34

⇒ x = 10

⇒ Number of rabbits = 4 × 10 = 40

questions.question: The height of a right circular cylinder is three times its radius. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 3696 cm², then the volume of the cylinder is equal to ({taking } pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the cylinder = 3 × radius.

Curved surface area (CSA) = 3696 cm².

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × radius × height.

Volume of the cylinder = π × radius² × height.

**Calculation:**

Let radius = r and height = 3r.

CSA = 2 × π × r × height

CSA = 2 × 22/7 × r × 3r

3696 = 2 × 22/7 × r × 3r

⇒ 3696 = 22/7 × r²

⇒ r² = (3696 × 7)/132

⇒ r² = 25872/132

⇒ r² = 196

⇒ r = 14 cm

Height = 3 × r = 3 × 14 = 42 cm

Volume = π × r² × height

Volume = 22/7× 14² × 42\)

Volume = 22/7 × 196 × 42

Volume = (22 × 8232)/7

Volume = 25872 cm³

**The volume of the cylinder is 25872 cm³.**

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
questions.solution:

Rate of Interest (R) = 9% per year

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

questions.question: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg and 35 kg is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Weights of five family members = 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg, and 35 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Average weight = Sum of all weights / Total number of members

**Calculation:**

Sum of all weights = 40 + 49 + 56 + 68 + 35

⇒ Sum of all weights = 248 kg

Total number of members = 5

Average weight = 248 / 5

⇒ Average weight = 49.6 kg

**The average weight of the family is 49.6 kg.**

questions.question: The average of the numbers 253, 245, 325, 120 and 115+2K is 212. Find the average of the numbers 353, 354, 225, 220 and 110+3K.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 253, 245, 325, 120, 115 + 2K

Average of these numbers = 212

Numbers for second part: 353, 354, 225, 220, 110 + 3K

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of Numbers) / (Number of Items)

**Calculation:**

Find the value of K using the given average for the first set of numbers.

Sum of first set of numbers = 253 + 245 + 325 + 120 + (115 + 2K)

⇒ Sum = 1058 + 2K

Average = Sum / 5

⇒ 212 = (1058 + 2K) / 5

⇒ 1058 + 2K = 212 × 5

⇒ 1058 + 2K = 1060

⇒ 2K = 1060 - 1058

⇒ 2K = 2

⇒ K = 1

Use K = 1 to find the average for the second set of numbers.

Numbers: 353, 354, 225, 220, (110 + 3K)

⇒ Numbers = 353, 354, 225, 220, (110 + 3 × 1)

⇒ Numbers = 353, 354, 225, 220, 113

Sum = 353 + 354 + 225 + 220 + 113

⇒ Sum = 1265

Average = Sum / 5

⇒ Average = 1265 / 5

⇒ Average = 253

**The average of the numbers is 253.**

questions.question: The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are 20 cm and 23 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the two diagonals of the rhombus:

Diagonal 1 = 20 cm.

Diagonal 2 = 23 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × Product of diagonals

**Calculation:**

Area = (1/2) × Diagonal 1 × Diagonal 2

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 20 × 23

⇒ Area = 10 × 23

⇒ Area = 230 cm²

**The area of the rhombus is 230 cm².**

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹19.5, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹19.5

Profit Percentage = 10%

Required Profit Percentage = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit Percentage/100)

New Selling Price (SPₙₑw) = CP × (1 + Required Profit Percentage/100)

Increase in Selling Price = SPₙₑw - SP

**Calculation:**

CP = SP / (1 + Profit Percentage/100)

⇒ CP = 19.5 / (1 + 10/100)

⇒ CP = 19.5 / 1.1

⇒ CP = 17.73

SPₙₑw = CP × (1 + Required Profit Percentage/100)

⇒ SPₙₑw = 17.73 × (1 + 50/100)

⇒ SPₙₑw = 17.73 × 1.5

⇒ SPₙₑw = 26.60

Increase in Selling Price = SPₙₑw - SP

⇒ Increase = 26.60 - 19.5

⇒ Increase = 7.09

**The dealer should increase the selling price by ₹7.09 to make a profit of 50%.**

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 13 km/h and the speed of the stream is 4 km/h. How much more time will it take in going upstream than in going downstream a distance of 68 km? (Correct to the nearest minute)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the boat in still water = 13 km/h.

Speed of the stream = 4 km/h.

Distance = 68 km.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed.

Speed upstream = (Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream).

Speed downstream = (Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream).

**Calculation:**

Speed upstream = 13 - 4 = 9 km/h.

Speed downstream = 13 + 4 = 17 km/h.

Time taken upstream = 68 / 9.

⇒ Time taken upstream = 7.555... hours.

Time taken downstream = 68 / 17.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 4 hours.

Difference in time = Time taken upstream - Time taken downstream.

⇒ Difference in time = 7.555... - 4 = 3.555... hours.

Convert 3.555... hours to minutes.

⇒ Difference in time = 3 hours + (0.555... × 60) minutes.

⇒ Difference in time = 3 hours + 33.33 minutes ≈ 3 hours 33 minutes.

**The correct option is 3 (3 hours 33 minutes).**

questions.question: The marked price of a chair is ₹1,800 and a discount of 18% is offered on the marked price. What additional discount must be offered to the customer now to bring the net price to ₹1,220? (Correct to two places of decimals.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price of the chair = ₹1,800

Discount offered = 18%

Net Price required = ₹1,220

**Formula Used:**

Net Price = Marked Price × (1 - First Discount) × (1 - Additional Discount)

To find Additional Discount:

Additional Discount = 1 - (Net Price / (Marked Price × (1 - First Discount)))

**Calculation:**

First Discount = 18% = 0.18

Step 1: Calculate the price after the first discount:

Price after First Discount = 1800 × (1 - 0.18)

⇒ Price after First Discount = 1800 × 0.82

⇒ Price after First Discount = ₹1,476

Step 2: Use the formula to find the Additional Discount:

Additional Discount = 1 - (Net Price / Price after First Discount)

⇒ Additional Discount = 1 - (1220 / 1476)

⇒ Additional Discount = 1 - 0.8265

⇒ Additional Discount = 0.1735

Step 3: Correct to two decimal places:

Additional Discount = 0.1734

**The additional discount required is 0.1734 (or 17.34%).**

questions.question:
The bar graph below shows the sale of books (in thousands) from five branches of a publishing company during 2008 and 2009.

What is the ratio of the total sale of books from the branches B1, B2 and B5 in 2009 to the total sale of books from the branches B2, B3, B4 and B5 in 2008?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6224c0ba450ffbc25eecfba6087131b89e38eff857ebc92762cba82e79562796.png]
questions.solution:

Sale of books in 2009:

B1 = 80, B2 = 60, B5 = 40

Sale of books in 2008:

B2 = 50, B3 = 70, B4 = 90, B5 = 60

**Formula Used:**

Ratio = Total sale in 2009 from branches B1, B2, and B5 / Total sale in 2008 from branches B2, B3, B4, and B5

**Calculation:**

Total sale in 2009 from B1, B2, and B5 = 80 + 60 + 40

Total sale in 2009 = 80 + 60 + 40 = 180

Total sale in 2008 from B2, B3, B4, and B5 = 50 + 70 + 90 + 60

Total sale in 2008 = 50 + 70 + 90 + 60 = 270

Ratio = Total sale in 2009 / Total sale in 2008

Ratio = 180 / 270

Simplify:

⇒ Ratio = 2 / 3

⇒ Ratio = 32 : 45

**Final Answer:**

The correct ratio is 32:45.

questions.question:
The average weight of a class of 115 students is 52.4 kg. If the average weight of the 63 boys is 60 kg, then find the average weight (in kg) of the girls in the class.

(Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of the class = 52.4 kg

Total students in the class = 115

Average weight of boys = 60 kg

Total boys = 63

Total girls = 115 - 63 = 52

**Formula Used:**

Average weight = Total weight / Total number of students

Total weight = Average weight × Total number of students

**Calculation:**

Total weight of the class = 52.4 × 115

⇒ Total weight of the class = 6026 kg

Total weight of boys = 60 × 63

⇒ Total weight of boys = 3780 kg

Total weight of girls = Total weight of the class - Total weight of boys

⇒ Total weight of girls = 6026 - 3780

⇒ Total weight of girls = 2246 kg

Average weight of girls = Total weight of girls / Total number of girls

⇒ Average weight of girls = 2246 / 52

⇒ Average weight of girls = 43.2 kg

**The average weight of the girls in the class is 43.2 kg.**

questions.question: In a circular race of 1500 m, P and Q start from the same point and at the same time, at speeds of 20 km/h and 35 km/h, respectively. After what time will they meet for the first time on the track if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance of the circular track = 1500 m

Speed of P = 20 km/h = (20 × 1000) / 3600 = 50 / 9 m/s

Speed of Q = 35 km/h = (35 × 1000) / 3600 = 175 / 18 m/s

**Formula Used:**

Time for the first meeting = Circumference of the track / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed (since they are running in the same direction) = Speed of Q - Speed of P

Relative Speed = (175 / 18) - (50 / 9)

Relative Speed = (175 / 18) - (100 / 18)

Relative Speed = (75 / 18)

Relative Speed = 25 / 6 m/s

Time for the first meeting = 1500 / (25 / 6)

⇒ Time = 1500 × (6 / 25)

⇒ Time = 9000 / 25

⇒ Time = 360 seconds

**The time after which P and Q will meet for the first time is 360 seconds.**
